correctness.rationale: The N-step clipped storage map contracts by at most r^N, providing a unique attracting periodic state. The reduced two-pulse fixed-point equations yield exhaustive no-overflow, one-overflow, and two-overflow regimes with exact threshold p0 and p1. Their runoff formulas combine into a max of zero and two explicit expressions. Each nonzero expression decreases strictly with the shorter cyclic gap; their maximum is nonincreasing and strictly decreases whenever the larger-gap schedule has positive runoff. Exact rational program reproduces 42,600 parameter/gap cases, verified recurrence equations and boundary examples; finite computations are supporting evidence rather than general proof.

originality.rationale: The assessed object is an exact deterministic infinite-horizon cyclic placement classification for two equal pulses, not the established stochastic runoff-distribution, threshold-triggering, or flood-frequency problems. Three particularly relevant full primary texts address random rainfall event statistics, synthetic stochastic storm time series, or flood return-period curves, and do not provide or directly imply the deterministic gap-indexed max-of-three formula, both event onset thresholds, and their exact ordering. The 1993 analytic soil-water storage source is publicly accessible at abstract level only. Broad fluid-queue and input-majorization antecedents remain a residual priority risk, so originality is provisional and not independently certified.
residual_risks: A general periodic finite-buffer, deterministic queue or majorization theorem outside the inspected hydrological literature may imply the gap ordering; historical priority not independently established.
The 1993 foundational Milly paper full text could not be accessed; the comparison is limited to the dated abstract and a detailed later paper describing its methodology.
One-store exponentially draining discrete dynamics are a deliberate hydrological idealization; broader field significance would require physical validation.

value.rationale: The result gives a complete exact schedule-selection rule over all placements of two equal storms in a repeated cycle, reveals precisely when a one-storm overflow changes to two-storm overflow, and provides a sharp, parameter-dependent no-runoff regime. For the same total rainfall and storage parameters, clustered storms yield 9/64 capacity units of runoff while less clustered schedules yield none. This nontrivial qualitative boundary is directly meaningful as a benchmark for nonlinear saturation-excess water-balance processes; no unrealistic claim about field flood peaks is made.
